adr02.Title: ADR-02 Scale telemetry ingestion with stateless services, farm-partitioned storage and asynchronous accepted-reading events
adr02.Context: Scalability is a driving QA: OzAgriMate must grow from 5,000 to over 50,000 farms, and seasonal events can multiply telemetry tenfold. ASR1 targets ingestion below two seconds, and C3 means gateways replay up to 72 hours of buffered readings after outages. Alternatives: synchronous fan-out, where ingestion calls irrigation, alerts and AI before responding, ties ingestion latency and capacity to every consumer; one vertically scaled database caps growth and creates a hot spot; per-farm deployments are unmanageable for at most eight engineers (C4). Replay storms must not crowd out live readings.
adr02.Decision: Run Telemetry as stateless, horizontally scaled instances, autoscaled on request rate and broker lag. Acknowledge a reading once stored, then publish a ReadingAccepted event through an outbox to the managed broker, partitioned by farmId, so consumers scale independently. Partition the time-series store by farm and observation time; every query is farm-scoped and capped at 500 rows. Idempotent reading IDs make replay retries safe, and replay traffic is rate-limited below live traffic. The prototype implements farm partitions, bounded queries, idempotent ingestion and the outbox; autoscaling and the broker are not deployed.
adr02.Consequences: Capacity grows by adding instances and partitions, and slow consumers cannot delay acknowledgements. Consumers see eventual consistency and must deduplicate events. Outbox, broker and partition management add cost and monitoring effort. Very active farms can create hot partitions. In-memory prototype results do not demonstrate production throughput.
adr02.Compliance: Load-test 50,000 simulated farms at tenfold peak with 72-hour replay: p95 acknowledgement under one second, zero lost readings. Alert when consumer lag exceeds 60 seconds.

adr06.Title: ADR-06 Adopt a versioned, idempotent JSON reading contract over HTTPS between Farm Edge Gateways and Telemetry
adr06.Context: Farms use heterogeneous sensors and field protocols such as LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, ISOBUS and vendor JSON, and rural links drop often. Telemetry needs one stable input it can validate, and gateways must resend buffered readings safely after outages (C3). ASR16 requires versioned APIs. Alternatives: accepting every vendor format in the cloud spreads protocol logic into Telemetry and changes it whenever hardware changes; devices publishing MQTT directly to a cloud broker need per-device credentials at large scale and bypass central validation; binary formats such as Protocol Buffers save bandwidth but are harder for partners to adopt and test.
adr06.Decision: Gateways translate field protocols locally and POST one canonical JSON reading per request to /farms/{farmId}/telemetry over HTTPS with a farm-bound machine credential. Each reading carries schemaVersion, a stable gateway-assigned readingId, deviceId, paddockId, metric, value, canonical unit and UTC observedAt. Telemetry rejects unknown versions, extra fields and unit mismatches with 422, returns 201 for new readings, 200 for identical replays and 409 for conflicting reuse. ReadingAccepted events reuse these fields. New schema versions are added alongside old ones, never changed in place.
adr06.Consequences: Telemetry stays protocol-agnostic, and replays never duplicate readings or downstream actions. Gateways must maintain adapters and stable reading IDs. Per-reading JSON costs more bandwidth than binary batches; batching is a candidate for a later version. Supporting several schema versions adds testing and deprecation effort.
adr06.Compliance: Contract tests verify 201, 200, 409 and 422 behaviour for each schema version. Gateway certification checks unit mapping and readingId stability before field deployment.

runtime_explanation: Gateway submits normalised reading; Telemetry authorises, validates, de-duplicates and classifies it, stores it, then publishes accepted readings asynchronously.
